papers.title: ChondroMap: A Spatially Resolved Framework for Quantifying the Mechanical Exposure Between Cartilage and Bone Surfaces in Knee Osteoarthritis
papers.abstract: Objective: This study presents ChondroMap, a spatially resolved framework for quantifying articulating cartilage- and bone-based contact interactions, demonstrated across various knee osteoarthritis (OA) severities. Design: Through probing the interactions between segmented high-resolution, spatially resolved cartilage/bone MRI scans and articulating kinematics from biplanar video-radiography (BVR), the ChondroMap framework aggregates cartilage-on-cartilage (CoC), cartilage-on-bone (CoB), and bone-on-bone (BoB) interactions to form a cumulative heatmap of mechanical exposure. To illustrate the framework, three participants representing mild, moderate, and severe knee OA underwent non-weight-bearing MRI to segment femoral and tibial bone and cartilage surfaces, followed by tracking BVR (30Hz) during level walking. ChondroMaps of registered kinematic and morphological data aggregated the articulating mechanical interactions throughout the activity cycle. Results: Application of the ChondroMap framework to the 3 participants revealed articular interaction patterns that varied markedly with severity. In the mild case, cumulative CoC strain was confined to a compact lateral region with minimal CoB and no BoB contact. The moderate case showed the greatest coexistence of all three interaction modes, including femoral- and tibial-sided CoB interactions and substantial medial BoB contact (up to 40%) adjacent to cartilage-related strain. The severe case showed consolidation into broad medial BoB regions (up to 65%), with high strains confined to the margins of denuded areas. Conclusion: ChondroMap presents a framework to capture the magnitude, duration, and spatial distribution of cartilage- and bone-based tibiofemoral interactions across complete activity cycles, offering a promising basis for mechanistic characterization of the articular environment in knee OA, particularly in advanced or heterogeneous degeneration.

papers.title: SPECTRAM: three-dimensional full-vector simulation of coherence-tunable microscopy images
papers.abstract: We present SPECTRAM, a physics-based framework for three-dimensional simulation of coherence-tunable microscopy image formation. Combining finite-difference time-domain solutions of Maxwell's equations with a coherence-tunable, polarization-dependent image-formation model, SPECTRAM captures full-vector light scattering and modality-specific optical processing in brightfield, differential interference contrast, and phase-contrast microscopy. It supports arbitrary three-dimensional sample geometries and generates volumetric image stacks under configurable illumination and objective parameters. Validated against Mie theory and experimental images of polystyrene beads, SPECTRAM further reproduces imaging features of an iPSC-derived stem cell using a refractive-index distribution estimated by gradient light interference microscopy. SPECTRAM provides a versatile, physics-based tool for quantitative three-dimensional simulation of phase-sensitive microscopy.

papers.title: Programming Continuous, High Framerate, and Long-Duration Data Acquisitions on the Verasonics Ultrasound System
papers.abstract: The ultrasound community has seen a rise in popularity of highly demanding imaging acquisition sequences, such as those for super-resolution ultrasound localization microscopy and functional ultrasound imaging, which push the boundary of ultrasound system hardware limits. However, subtle errors in sequence programming can lead to corrupted data, inaccurate timing, and slow data throughput, which impact the performance of these modalities. In this article, we detail the fundamentals of the hardware and software sequencers for the Verasonics Vantage/NXT research ultrasound scanner, highlighting some common pitfalls in sequence design and ways to overcome them. We include example imaging sequences for different data acquisition goals, and detail recommended ways to test these sequences to ensure that they are meeting the expected performance.

papers.title: Simulation-based inference of a multiscale reversible-electroporation model reveals how population variability shapes atrial cardioversion
papers.abstract: Electrical therapies remain a cornerstone for terminating cardiac arrhythmia, but they are painful, require sedation, and may fail in complex cases. Reversible electroporation, traditionally seen as an unwanted side effect of electrical stimulation, may itself help terminate arrhythmia. However, its dual and potentially proarrhythmic effects remain poorly understood and largely unexplored in silico. We therefore developed and calibrated a multiscale computational model of human atrial electroporation using a population-of-models approach.In vitro recordings from rat cardiomyocytes were processed into action potential and calcium transient biomarkers and compared across control (no high-voltage pulse), non-electroporated (high-voltage pulse, no electroporation signs), and electroporated cells. We extended a human atrial cell model with a Goldman-Hodgkin-Katz electroporation leak current, electroporation-induced ion channel damage, and a sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium overload release mechanism, which reproduced the observed calcium oscillations. The model was calibrated across a population of cells using simulation-based inference. The number of pores was the most identifiable parameter, followed by the characteristic pore resealing time and the inward rectifier potassium conductance. The fast sodium, L-type calcium and sodium-calcium exchanger conductances were only weakly identified. Four representative phenotypes were then used in two-dimensional tissue simulations of reentry. Increasing the number of pores slowed the reentry, then terminated it, and finally caused depolarization block, although the doses required varied across phenotypes. Electroporation-induced reduction of conduction velocity either facilitated cardioversion or promoted reentry, depending on the phenotype and the number of pores.By integrating multiple electroporation mechanisms with population-level calibration, and by translating findings from rat to human and from cell to tissue, this framework provides a mechanistic platform to investigate how electroporation can both terminate and promote arrhythmias. It offers a basis for designing future in vitro experiments and electroporation-based approaches for human cardiac electrical therapy.

papers.title: The allometry of ground reaction forces in Atta vollenweideri leaf-cutter ants.
papers.abstract: As animals get larger, their weight increases faster than the cross-sectional area of geometrically similar muscles. How, then, do the forces exerted by individual legs change with body size to keep up with this demand? We measured three-dimensional ground reaction forces exerted by individual legs of freely walking leaf-cutter ants (Atta vollenweideri), sampling workers across a fivefold range in body mass. Forelegs exerted the largest peak vertical and propulsive forces, whereas midlegs exerted the largest braking forces. Vertical force further increased most steeply in the midlegs, so that the midleg peak approached the foreleg peak in larger workers. Across 49 insect and vertebrate species spanning nine orders of magnitude in body mass, peak vertical force, adjusted for limb number and accounting for phylogeny, increased almost in direct proportion to mass. Although these species differ vastly in phylogenetic history, body size, and leg number, peak force thus keeps pace with body weight, permitting locomotion at similar duty factors. We suggest that in-series elasticity can help explain how peak forces in dynamic contractions can scale this steeply across many decades, even in geometrically similar animals.

papers.title: Transient mRNA-LNP Delivery of the Tardigrade Protein Dsup Protects Airway Epithelium from Bleomycin-Induced Injury
papers.abstract: Bleomycin is an essential component of chemotherapy regimens used for Hodgkin lymphoma and germ cell tumors, but its clinical utility is restricted by pulmonary toxicity that forces dose reduction or discontinuation in around 10% of patients. There are currently no approved strategies that prophylactically protect the lungs, representing a significant unmet clinical need. Bleomycin generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) within the alveolar epithelium, causing alveolar cell death and senescence and driving maladaptive crosstalk with stromal cells. Tardigrades are extremophilic organisms that can survive high levels of ROS. This is in part through expression of the tardigrade-specific Damage suppressor (Dsup) protein, which interacts with chromatin and shields the tardigrade genome from ROS. Induction of Dsup expression has been shown to protect human epithelia from radiation-induced injury, and because radiation and bleomycin share ROS generation as their principal cytotoxic mechanism, we hypothesized that this protection may extend to chemoprotection within the alveolar epithelium. We therefore asked whether transient, non-integrating Dsup expression delivered by messenger RNA lipid nanoparticles (mRNA-LNPs) could protect lung epithelium during the window of drug exposure. We employed an LNP formulation that retained its physicochemical properties after nebulization and produced lung-restricted reporter expression after intratracheal administration in mice. Additionally, the same formulation successfully transfected human and porcine air-liquid-interface cultures. Dsup-GFP mRNA transfection produced nuclear-restricted expression in A549 and primary human small airway epithelial cells (HSAECs) that peaked at 24 hours and returned to background by day 5, with no effect on proliferation before or after clearance. Central to its potential chemoprotective role, Dsup mRNA LNP pretreatment significantly reduced bleomycin-induced DNA damage and senescence in both cell types. These results establish transient mRNA-delivered Dsup as a feasible epithelial chemoprotective strategy and define a delivery platform compatible with inhaled administration.

papers.title: Scalable direct mapping of signal-transduction dynamics using protein-assembly recorders
papers.abstract: The timing and coordination of signaling events within signal-transduction cascades shape cellular behavior. Protein-assembly recorders empower signaling dynamics study by scalable spatiotemporal mapping of downstream transcriptional outputs, yet we still lack a general mechanism to directly write signal-transduction dynamics. Here we introduce SPLITR, a modular strategy that writes protein-protein interactions and associated signaling dynamics directly into growing protein assemblies for retrospective readout, through proximity-mediated split-intein trans-splicing and reconstitution of assembly-competent reporters. SPLITR achieves up to 334-fold dynamic range in a membrane-tethered configuration and functions across structurally distinct scaffolds. Ca2+ and multiple kinase activities can be recorded using validated sensing modules. In cultured cells, Ca2+ and protein kinase A (PKA) recorders retain transient stimulation events and report signal activation with negligible latency and sub-hour temporal error. In mouse tumors, SPLITR preserves chemically evoked Ca2+ activity and resolves its timing. Multiplexed Ca2+ and PKA recording writes two signaling histories within a shared scaffold. Coupling the multiplexed recorder to automated laboratory enables scalable profiling of a compound library, revealing differences in response amplitude and temporal features. SPLITR extends assembly recording from transcriptional outputs to molecular interactions and interaction-mediated signaling, unlocking scalable tracking of a broad panel of signal-transduction dynamics in space and time.

papers.title: High-resolution omics and functional profiling of fatty-acid-driven metabolic modulation reveal enhanced physiological relevance of engineered heart tissues
papers.abstract: Background: Human pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hPSC-CMs) hold vast potential for cardiovascular disease modeling and drug discovery, yet their immaturity limits their ability to recapitulate adult cardiac physiology. Three-dimensional engineered heart tissues (3D-EHTs) provide a functional and more physiologically-relevant model for disease modeling and drug screening. However, EHTs typically retain an immature metabolic phenotype. To further enhance maturation, we investigated how fatty acid (FA) supplementation and physiological insulin concentrations influence metabolic maturation and its consequences for cardiac function, pharmacological responses, and hypoxic injury. Methods: The effects of FA and insulin supplementation on 3D-EHT maturation were investigated using an integrated molecular and functional approach. Four medium variations were evaluated through functional tests, calcium handling assays, immunofluorescence, ATP quantification, gene expression analysis, high-resolution proteomics, and metabolomics to relate metabolic remodeling to tissue function and responses to pharmacological and hypoxic challenges. Results: FA supplementation enhanced the metabolic maturation of EHTs, surpassing the maturation achieved with an already highly specialized cardiomyocyte medium. The combination of FA with physiological insulin concentrations promoted a shift toward oxidative metabolism, supported by metabolic profiling and associated molecular changes identified through proteomic analysis. This metabolic remodeling was accompanied by changes in contractile performance and calcium handling, altered responses to clinically relevant pharmacological agents, and increased susceptibility to hypoxic injury. Notably, drug concentration-response relationships shifted toward clinically relevant exposure ranges for several compounds. Together, these findings establish a link between metabolic maturation, molecular remodeling, and functional responses of 3D cardiac tissues to pharmacological and pathological challenges. Conclusions: Our findings demonstrate that metabolic culture conditions influence not only the maturation state of hPSC-CMs in 3D-EHTs but also their responses to drugs and hypoxic stress. By integrating multi-omics profiling with functional and disease-relevant assessments, this study provides a framework for improving the physiological relevance of engineered cardiac tissues for disease modeling and preclinical drug evaluation.

papers.title: Individual gait is not the optimum of standard cost functions: a test with two predictive simulation frameworks
papers.abstract: Background: Predictive simulations of gait are increasingly proposed as a way to predict how individuals, including people with impaired gait, will walk. Most approaches generate gait by minimising a cost function, a weighted sum of terms such as metabolic energy and muscle activation. The weights of the cost can be personalised using inverse optimal control (IOC), but the basic assumption that an individual's gait is the optimum of a cost is rarely questioned or tested. Methods: We tested this assumption on the openly available data of healthy adults with subject-scaled models, using a shooting framework with a reflex controller (implemented in SCONE) and a direct collocation framework (implemented in PredSim). For each individual, we compared a simulation that tracked the measured joint angles, electromyography and stride time with the gaits that minimised the framework's standard cost at 35 weightings. We repeated the comparison for averages of 10 to 30 subjects. Paired comparisons across the 20 subjects used the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, and averages were compared with the mean of their members by generalised least squares. Results: In both frameworks, the standard-cost optimum tracked the data worse than the tracked gait in every subject, and the tracked gait always had a higher cost. Reweighting lowered the tracking error of the optimum, but the best weighting still tracked the data worse than the tracked gait in both frameworks. When the data and bodies of subjects were averaged, the standard-cost optimum of the average tracked the averaged data 30% more closely than individual optima tracked individual data. Conclusions: Changing the weights of cost function elements only selects a different optimum of the same cost terms, whereas individual gait, as represented by the tracked gait, was not an optimum of the standard cost. The closer match between optima and averaged data suggests that comparisons with group data overstate how well standard costs describe individuals. Predicting individual gait therefore requires formulations that allow the simulated gait to deviate from the optimum of a cost.

papers.title: Osmium Tetroxide-Enhanced μCT Enables 3D Mapping of Intra-articular Adipose Tissue
papers.abstract: Objectives: Intra-articular adipose tissue is a unique adipose depot that has received increasing attention in the context of osteoarthritis pathophysiology, but no robust methodologies currently exist for its 3D visualization and quantification in preclinical models. This study developed a protocol for visualization and quantification of intra-articular adipose tissue in murine knee joints using osmium tetroxide (OsTet)-based contrast-enhanced micro-computed tomography (CT), followed by illustration of its utility to assess adipose remodeling in a murine post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) model. Design: Systematic optimization of sample preparation, OsTet incubation conditions, and CT acquisition parameters was conducted to establish a protocol tailored for murine knee joints. PTOA was induced via non-invasive anterior cruciate ligament rupture to demonstrate the utility of this protocol in the assessment of disease-associated remodeling. Results: Optimization of our OsTet-enhanced CT protocol overcame attenuation artifacts and incomplete penetrance in intra-articular adipose depots of the murine knee. Adjusting acquisition parameters (0.10 mm Cu filter, 90 kVp) mitigated beam hardening and resolved tissue heterogeneity. Complete tissue penetration and uptake equilibrium were achieved using a 1% OsTet concentration incubated for 48 h in both healthy and injured limbs. Applied to a PTOA model, the pipeline reliably detected microstructural adipose remodeling, with low signal regions corresponding to fibrotic tissue, which was validated by histopathological staining. Conclusions: This study established OsTet-enhanced CT as a reliable imaging method for joint-wide assessment of adipose remodeling, providing a valuable framework for future studies investigating the role of joint adipose tissue in development, homeostasis, and disease.

papers.title: A one-pot workflow for spatial proteomicsaided by ShapeX
papers.abstract: The rapid growth in instrumental sensitivity has enabled deep proteomic profiling of small tissue regions, increasing the availability and interest in spatial proteomics. However, sample preparation remains a practical bottleneck, as any additional clean-up and transfer steps increase losses of already limited material. Here, we developed a onepot workflow in which laser-microdissected tissue is collected, de-crosslinked, and digested in the same well, followed by direct injection for liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry. We first evaluated the de-crosslinking and digestion across different tissue inputs. Heating at 95 {degrees}C for 15 minutes provided a practical balance between proteome coverage and processing time, reducing the heating period by 75% relative to a 60-minute incubation. Using this condition, we quantified a mean of 2,751, 3,237, 3,786, and 5,046 protein groups from 1,000, 2,000, 5,000, and 10,000 m2 regions, respectively, without match-between-runs. We next evaluated 1,536-well plates for higher-throughput tissue collection and sample preparation. Following transfer for LC-MS analysis, the strongest proteomic signals generally coincided with the intended collection wells, indicating that tissue collection in this format is feasible. In parallel, we developed ShapeX, a QuPath extension that links tissue annotation to laser microdissection and plate-based sample preparation through customizable plate layouts, annotation tessellation, and coordinated export of sampling and dispensing files. We used ShapeX to map proteomic measurements back to the original tissue regions in two intestinal experiments. Spatial reconstruction recovered opposing gradients in proteins associated with epithelial differentiation and replication and distinguished the sampled glandular epithelium from adjacent stroma. Together, the one-pot preparation and ShapeX provide a practical workflow for image-guided spatial proteomics, from tissue annotation and sample collection to spatial mapping of protein abundance.

papers.title: Towards a Physiologically Rigorous Heartbeat Dynamics Foundation Model
papers.abstract: Capturing long-range heartbeat dynamics accurately from wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings is a key challenge in personalized healthcare and autonomic neuroscience. Although classical methods are physiologically grounded and statistically rigorous, they cannot learn across population data and therefore cannot scale. Time series foundation models, on the other hand, can scale, but fail to capture physiologically meaningful beat-to-beat dynamics. We present, to our knowledge, the first probabilistic foundation model of heartbeat dynamics: a density-based neural temporal point process (NTPP) pretrained on RR-interval sequences from 11,226 subjects across five public datasets spanning normal sinus rhythm, arrhythmia, atrial fibrillation, and ischemia. We establish a physiological scaling law in this domain, showing that held-out metrics improve predictably with cohort size. We additionally show that scaling behavior in stochastic output domains like physiology should be evaluated by distributional calibration metrics (KS distance, goodness-of-fit) rather than point-error (MAE, RMSE), because point errors approach their irreducible floor while distributional properties continue to improve. Our pretrained model transfers zero-shot to a held-out ambulatory dataset, reaching 94.7% goodness-of-fit with no subject-specific data. In 5-minute autoregressive simulation, the model remains calibrated (87-88% goodness-of-fit) and generates trajectories with real physiological variability. Finally, we show that the learned representations are physiologically interpretable. The recurrent history embeddings separate normal and arrhythmia windows in held-out test subjects with a balanced accuracy of 95.7%. The lognormal mixture distributions show that arrhythmia subjects differ mainly in predictive spread (3.5x larger standard deviation than normal cohort), with only a small shift toward shorter mean RR than the normal group (0.79 vs. 0.86s). These results establish population-scale pretraining as a foundation for physiologically grounded modeling and simulation of heartbeat dynamics.

papers.title: Shear stress magnitude affects bacterial extracellular vesicle stimulation of endothelial cells
papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles released by pathogenic bacteria can induce strong inflammatory cascades, in part, by upregulating adhesion molecules on the surface of endothelial cells. The adhesion molecules support immune cell attachment and migration into surrounding tissues, amplifying local and systemic inflammation in conditions such as sepsis. We and others have predominantly studied the role of bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) in tissue barrier models and microphysiological systems (MPS) under static conditions. Here, we investigated how physiological levels of fluid shear stress affect endothelial stimulation by Escherichia coli-derived BEVs. Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) were exposed to BEVs, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), or untreated medium under static, low-shear (1.5 dyn/cm2), and high-shear (10 dyn/cm2) conditions, while increases in the surface expression of intercellular adhesion molecule-1 (ICAM-1) were measured. BEVs elicited greater ICAM-1 expression than LPS under both low- and high-shear conditions, suggesting endothelial responses to BEVs depend on both the stimulus and mechanical environment. Although the highest absolute ICAM-1 expression occurred under high shear, the largest relative response to BEVs occurred under low shear. Together, these data show that hemodynamic shear stress is a critical determinant of BEV-associated endothelial inflammatory responses and a critical element for vascular MPS devices modeling conditions such as sepsis.

papers.title: Structural Metrics from Predicted Protein-Ligand Complexes Enable OATP Inhibitor Classification
papers.abstract: Organic anion transporting polypeptides (OATPs) mediate the cellular uptake of many clinically important drugs, and their inhibition can alter drug disposition and contribute to drug-drug interactions. Recent advances in protein-ligand co-folding have expanded opportunities for modeling transporters and their interactions with diverse small molecules. However, the extent to which these models can predict functional transporter inhibition remains unclear. Here, we systematically evaluated the predictive utility of structural metrics generated by AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, Chai-1, and Protenix using experimental inhibition measurements for 224 compounds across OATP1B1, OATP1B3, and OATP2B1. Individual structural metrics provided substantial inhibitor discrimination ability, reaching an ROC-AUC of 0.888 for Chai-1 structures of OATP1B3. We then investigated whether integrating multiple structural descriptors improves inhibitor classification relative to optimized individual metrics, which improved performances in many model-OATP combinations. Following combined-metric analysis, Protenix exhibited both the highest absolute average precision (AP) and the largest improvement in AP overall for OATP1B1 (0.560 to 0.763). Mean improvements persisted across five independently generated cross validation partitions. Performance and the benefits of metric integration differed across transporters and modeling pipelines, while increasing structural ensemble size for each drug from 1 to 100 provided varied improvements. Together, these findings establish the utility of co-folding structural metrics as functional classification features, and this work establishes a framework for evaluating and integrating structure-prediction outputs in broader functional studies of membrane transporters.

papers.title: Cyst-like intraluminal hyaluronic acid accumulation inhibits breast epithelial cell invasion via pressure-driven ECM compaction
papers.abstract: While elevated hyaluronic acid (HA) biosynthesis by breast epithelial cells is implicated in tumorigenesis, HA can also contribute to benign tissue remodeling, including mammary morphogenesis and lumen formation in embryogenesis. What determines whether HA drives malignant invasion or benign remodeling remains unclear. To investigate, we embedded spheroids of HA synthase (HAS)-overexpressing breast epithelial cells in collagen hydrogels modeling dense breast stroma. Confocal and optical coherence microscopy showed that HAS overexpression produced different outcomes in single cells and spheroids: individual cells invaded into the collagen, whereas spheroids accumulated HA internally, causing osmotic swelling and hydrostatic pressure-driven lumen formation. An in silico cell-vertex model identified paracellular fluid flow as a mechanism of lumen formation, coinciding with confinement-induced reorganization of cell-cell adhesion strengths. In situ pressure sensors, confocal reflectance imaging, and finite element analysis showed that spheroid expansion compressed the surrounding collagen, inducing densification and a material phase transition that inhibited invasion. Co-culture and direct contact with matrix-remodeling stromal cells attenuated this effect and restored invasive potential. Although HA overproduction in single cells has been linked to malignancy, our findings identify a biophysical mechanism by which multicellular HA accumulation suppresses tumor invasion and show how stromal remodeling can override this protection. These results offer a potential explanation for the context-dependent relationship between fibrocystic breast changes and breast cancer risk.

papers.title: PFLISA: A New Ultrasensitive, Multiplex Immunoassay Platform Enables Cytokine Network Profiling in Sepsis
papers.abstract: Immune responses emerge from coordinated cytokine networks, but quantitative profiling remains constrained by limited clinical sample volumes and the very low circulating concentrations of many biologically important mediators. We introduce the Plasmonic Fluor-Linked ImmunoSorbent Assay (PFLISA), that combines plasmonic-enhanced fluorescence with spatially encoded antibody arrays in a standard 96-well format. PFLISA quantified 12 inflammatory cytokines in parallel from 15 L of plasma, with lower limits of quantification of 3.4-110 fg/mL and analyte-specific quantitative ranges spanning multiple orders of magnitude. Within-well replicate spots showed an average coefficient of variation of 5.7%, and 35 of 36 analyte-by-quality-control conditions exhibited intra- and interplate coefficients of variation below 20% across 16 plates. We applied the platform to plasma from 100 patients with sepsis and 97 healthy controls as a clinically demanding demonstration. Eleven of the 12 cytokines were significantly elevated in sepsis after false-discovery-rate correction. Pro- and anti-inflammatory composite scores increased 10.6-fold and 3.9-fold, respectively, yielding a 2.0-fold increase in their ratio and revealing concurrent but disproportionate activation of the two responses. Gram-negative infections were associated with higher IL-6, IL-8, TNF-, and IL-10 concentrations than Gram-positive infections. PFLISA thus brings low-abundance regulatory cytokines into the same patient-level profile as more abundant inflammatory mediators, increasing the portion of the immune network that can be quantitatively observed from limited clinical samples.

papers.title: Fighting Sleep: Minute-by-Minute Driver Fatigue from a Dry-Electrode EEG Headband
papers.abstract: Driver-facing cameras often catch fatigue too late. We asked whether a four-electrode dry headband, which picks up eye movements electrically and head tilt with a motion sensor, can follow fatigue minute by minute. Nine participants wore the headband for twelve sessions of a 50-minute monotonous task at a driving simulator station, without driving, answering one cue a minute and rating their sleepiness every five minutes, with a webcam on the face for comparison. An index built without training from blink length, slow eye movements and head tilt, read against each participant's own first eight minutes, followed fatigue beyond elapsed time across the nine participants (0.32, p = 0.002), above zero in eight of them and at zero in the ninth. With its alarm line set for a 10 percent false-positive rate on not-sleepy minutes, it caught 91 percent of the minutes rated as fighting sleep, where the standard camera eye-closure measure (PERCLOS, the share of each minute with the eyes at least 80 percent closed), set the same way on the same minutes, caught 33 percent (67 minutes from four participants). Averaged over the six recordings that reached fighting sleep, the index crossed its alarm line about three minutes before the first minute rated as fighting sleep; in the five sessions with video its alarm had sounded by then in four, where the camera's sounded 6 to 13 minutes after in four and never in the fifth. The index and its alarm were then fixed and taken into a car, on one outing by one participant. Through a 33-minute rested drive the headband returned a value for every minute and raised no alarm. With the car parked and the driver doing the laboratory task, its alarm sounded nine minutes before he fell asleep, as seen on video; the camera's, set the same way, came eight minutes later, with one minute to spare. Signal amplitude at the electrodes was no higher in the parked car than in the laboratory, and with the car moving the electrodes that carry the index stayed in range 99 percent of the time.

papers.title: A Full-Thickness 3D Bioprinted Melanoma-on-Chip Platform for Preclinical Therapeutic Testing
papers.abstract: Malignant melanoma remains a major clinical challenge due to its high metastatic potential and frequent therapy resistance. Although recent therapeutic advances have improved patient survival, predictive preclinical models that recapitulate the human tumor microenvironment (TME) remain limited. We developed a human 3D bioprinted melanoma-on-chip platform that combines a fully differentiated, barrier-forming human skin model with microfluidic perfusion and spatially controlled integration of melanoma spheroids at the epidermal-dermal junction. This provides a standardized tissue environment for longitudinal tumor and therapeutic studies for up to 21 days. To validate our model for preclinical therapeutic testing, we treated the melanoma-on-chip with the oncolytic virus VSV-GP. In 2D, viral infection of melanoma cells resulted in homogeneous cell death within 48 hours. In melanoma-on-chip, viral propagation was restricted to tumor cells and markedly delayed compared to 2D. Although VSV-GP stopped melanoma growth in 3D, it did not achieve complete tumor-cell eradication, as observed in 2D culture. These findings demonstrate that the 3D skin tissue environment substantially influences viral infection kinetics and therapeutic outcome, underscoring the need for more physiologically relevant human tissue models in preclinical drug evaluation.

papers.title: Single-cell Morphological Mechanisms-of-Action Profiling using Nanowell Imaging Plates
papers.abstract: Mechanism-of-action (MoA) analysis is used in drug discovery to prioritize compounds that act through desired pathways while eliminating compounds associated with nonspecific or undesirable activity. Image cytometry provides a promising route for MoA inference by capturing high-dimensional cellular phenotypes at single-cell resolution, but conventional workflows remain limited by unreliable cell segmentation and dependence on human-engineered feature extraction. Here, we present a deep learning-based image cytometry workflow that confines single cells in nanowells to obtain uniformly framed, regularized single-cell images, enabling MoA inference directly from raw images without segmentation or human-engineered features. Using a nanowell-in-microwell platform, we treated cells with 21 chemotherapeutic compounds spanning 11 MoA classes across multiple doses and time points, generating more than 500,000 single-cell images for model training and validation. A ResNet-18 convolutional neural network trained on images annotated by known compound mechanism achieved 85% accuracy in MoA classification. When a second model was trained on compound identity rather than MoA, misclassification patterns frequently linked compounds with shared mechanisms, indicating that the model learned mechanism-level relationships directly from single-cell morphology, without those relationships being specified in advance. Together, these results establish regularized single-cell imaging in nanowells as a scalable and interpretable approach to image-based MoA classification that overcomes key limitations of segmentation-dependent feature analysis.

papers.title: TEMPLE-MEASURED POSTPRANDIAL CARDIOVASCULAR RESPONSES UNDER FREE-LIVING CONDITIONS
papers.abstract: Eating perturbs cardiovascular homeostasis: splanchnic vasodilation after a meal is offset by autonomic adjustments that raise heart rate, and both the magnitude and duration of this response can depend on meal size and composition. Measuring these responses in daily life requires knowing when each meal begins and ends, which self-report captures poorly. The temple region allows both to be measured with a single device: chewing-related motion over the temporalis can mark meal onset and offset, and photoplethysmography (PPG) at the superficial temporal artery (STA) records the cardiovascular response. The STA also supplies a vascular bed whose postprandial behavior has not been well characterized. Using a temple-worn wearable under free-living conditions, we asked (1) whether established postprandial heart rate (HR) responses can be observed from automatically detected meals, and (2) how PPG pulse morphology at the STA changes after a meal. One meal from each of 100 participants in free-living conditions was analyzed, comparing a 15-min pre-meal baseline with the 120 min after eating, with nutrient content estimated from meal photographs. HR rose approximately 2.6 bpm on average in the first 15 min after eating and approached baseline within two hours. The postprandial rise in HR increased with caloric content. HR remained elevated two hours after the most sodium-dense meals, whereas higher fiber density was associated with a larger rise only during the first 15 minutes. The heart-rate increase per 100 kcal was greater in participants with higher BMI. In addition, the PPG morphology index A_d/A_a, a second-derivative PPG marker of vascular tone and wave reflection, increased within 15 minutes of the meal and remained shifted at two hours at the temple region. This change persisted after adjustment for heart rate and is consistent with reduced wave reflection, possibly associated with vasodilation in vessels downstream of the aorta. These results support the feasibility of using a single temple-worn device to detect meals and measure the cardiac and vascular responses that follow in daily life, and identify the temple as a site for studying postprandial vascular changes.

papers.title: Optimisation of GMP-compliant hollow-fiber culturing and scaled-up separation of mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles to overcome unexpected impact of bovine serum contaminants' transfer to end products
papers.abstract: The clinical translation of mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) requires scalable manufacturing strategies ensuring product purity, reproducibility, and compliance with Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) standards. However, fetal bovine serum (FBS)-derived contaminants may persist in EV preparations, compromising their characterization and clinical applicability. This study aimed to optimize MSC-EV production using hollow-fiber bioreactors while minimizing bovine protein contamination through improved culture and purification strategies. Extracellular vesicles from immortalized human adipose-derived MSCs were produced under different culture conditions, including FBS supplementation, partial replacement with Panexin, and use of chemically defined medium for high-density cultures (CDM-HD). EVs were purified using tangential flow filtration, fast protein liquid chromatography, and ultrafiltration, and characterized by nanoparticle tracking analysis, electron microscopy, Western blot, proteomics, and ELISA. Proteomic analysis revealed substantial bovine protein contamination under conventional FBS-containing conditions, with 11.4% of identified proteins exclusively assigned to bovine origin. Transitioning to CDM-HD reduced this proportion to 2.6%, markedly decreasing albumin abundance. Optimization of Panexin supplementation supported MSC expansion while reducing the necessary percentage of bovine serum. Although albumin became undetectable by Western blot, sensitive ELISA measurements revealed residual contamination and suggested unexpected protein carryover associated with chromatography column reuse. Importantly, using a new purification column yielded CDM-HD-derived EV preparations with albumin concentrations below ELISA assay's quantification limit (0.69 ng/mL). These findings highlight the importance of controlling both upstream culture conditions and downstream purification to prevent exogenous protein contamination, establishing a promising scalable manufacturing workflow for high-purity MSC-EVs suitable for further GMP-oriented development and future clinical translation.

papers.title: BMP-2 Release from Biomaterial Carriers: Reporting Heterogeneity and the Limits of Cross-Study Prediction
papers.abstract: Published release profiles offer a potential basis for predicting bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) delivery from biomaterial carriers, but heterogeneous reporting and study-specific effects complicate their reuse in machine learning (ML) models. As a preliminary exploration, we compiled 79 release experiments and 487 time points from 21 publications with a workflow that combined a large language model assistant and human verification, and we examined data comparability and cross-study prediction with ML models. Only 38 experiments (48%) reported BMP-2 alone as a percentage of the loaded dose. Within individual studies, binding components and coating layers were associated with slower release, consistent with established carrier mechanisms. Using carrier family as the sole predictor, a family-median model and gradient-boosted decision trees achieved lower mean absolute errors than a global-median baseline under random hold-out validation (0.42 and 0.44 versus 0.52 log10 units). Publication-grouped cross-validation did not establish a corresponding improvement (0.57 and 0.48 versus 0.50). Only 10 of the 28 modeling experiments belonged to carrier families represented in the training data under this scheme, and carrier family was strongly associated with publication. These findings highlight the need to distinguish within-study interpolation from cross-study generalization. Broader coverage of each carrier family, quantitative formulation and assay descriptors, and accessible numerical source data are needed to support predictive modeling of BMP-2 release.

papers.title: A One-Year In Vivo Study of a Braided Pure Molybdenum Stent: Favorable Biocompatibility and the Critical Challenge of Vascular Biomechanics
papers.abstract: Background: This study aims to evaluate a newly developed biodegradable stent made of pure Molybdenum (Mo) for treating intracranial aneurysms. Unlike traditional permanent metal stents that remain in the body indefinitely, this new device aims to provide temporary support during the healing process and then safely dissolve. Methods: A 30.48 {micro}m braided Mo stent was developed, and its mechanical performance and degradation process were tested in vitro. The stent was then implanted into the arteries of Beagle dogs for a one-year observation period. The study compared these new stents against standard non-degradable stents to monitor safety, structural changes, and the degradation rate within a living organism. Results: The Mo stents demonstrated excellent biocompatibility, showing no signs of organ damage or neurotoxicity, and the material degraded at a rate suitable for aneurysm healing (4.88-5.12 {micro}m/year). However, while the control stents held their shape, the Mo stents showed progressive structural deformation and recoil over time when implanted in the common carotid artery and subclavian artery of Beagle dogs. Conclusion: While this study confirms that Mo is a biocompatible material for stents, it highlights a major challenge in dynamic blood vessels. Future designs must focus on improving the stent's resistance to withstand the repetitive forces found in dynamic blood vessels before it can be considered for clinical use, and intracranial application still requires validation using aneurysm models in the future.

papers.title: RoWS Biofabrication of Neuromuscular Tubuloids from Human Neuromesodermal Progenitors
papers.abstract: Combining multicellular self-organization with defined tissue architecture remains a challenge in human neuromuscular modeling. Here, we use rotary wet-spinning (RoWS) biofabrication to encapsulate human neuromesodermal progenitors (NMPs) within fibrin-based cores surrounded by alginate shells, generating neuromuscular tubuloids (nmTubs). NMPs derived from a human embryonic stem cell and an induced pluripotent stem cell line were cultured for up to 50 days and assessed by gene expression analysis, immunofluorescence, tissue orientation measurements, and calcium imaging. Both cell lines generated muscle and neural compartments, with distinct differentiation kinetics and tissue proportions. Embryonic stem cell-derived nmTubs developed more extensive neural- and endothelial-associated structures and displayed spontaneous contractions from day 14 onward. Between days 30 and 50, muscle tissue area and myotube diameter increased, while acetylcholine receptor domains underwent spatial remodeling. Neural projections exhibited pronounced longitudinal organization within the constructs. Acetylcholine-associated calcium transients demonstrated tissue responsiveness, although functional neuromuscular transmission remains to be established. These findings show that RoWS can combine a common developmental progenitor population with a defined fibrous architecture to support multicellular neuromuscular development. nmTubs provide a platform to investigate the relationships among biomaterial geometry, tissue organization, and maturation in human neuromuscular models.

papers.title: A highly-parallel microchannel platform reveals the transcriptomic and epigenetic signature of confined migration
papers.abstract: Confining tissue microenvironments are ubiquitous in vivo, yet existing in vitro platforms are limited in geometric control, throughput, or compatibility with post-migration cell recovery. We developed a highly parallel microchannel membrane containing thousands of tunable microchannels in a format compatible with standard cell culture, imaging, cell retrieval, and direct lysis. The platform enables control over channel cross-sectional area, length, and geometry across multiple cell types. Using this system, we recovered sufficient post-confined cells for bulk RNA-seq and ATAC-seq, revealing confinement-dependent transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility signatures. Increasing confinement was associated with predominantly reduced chromatin accessibility, while comparison of two cancer cell lines identified shared differentially expressed genes and convergent enrichment of cancer-associated, inflammatory, and EMT-related pathways. This scalable platform enables omics-scale analysis of cells after migration through defined physical microenvironments.

papers.title: Plasma-Polymerized Polyurethane/Reduced Graphene Oxide Electrospun Patch for Cardiac Tissue Engineering
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Traditional treatments, including heart transplantation, are limited by the scarcity of donor organs and the need for lifelong immunosuppression, highlighting the urgent need for alternative therapies. Cardiac patches represent a promising approach to restoring heart function by providing structural support and promoting cardiac tissue regeneration. Here, we developed biocompatible and conductive electrospun cardiac patches, aiming to mimic the structural, mechanical, and electrical properties of the native myocardium. polyurethane (PU) was selected as the base material due to its favorable mechanical properties and biocompatibility. Reduced graphene oxide (rGO) was incorporated into the electrospun PU fibers to enhance electrical conductivity, and a low-pressure plasma-polymerized nitrogen-rich (LPPE:N) coating was applied to improve cell adhesion. The fabricated patches were characterized through various techniques, including scanning electron microscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, tensile testing, and conductivity measurements. Also, in vitro cytotoxicity assay using primary cardiac fibroblasts confirmed the biocompatibility of the patches. These physicochemical, electromechanical, and biological characterizations suggest that the rGO/LPPE:N-functionalized PU patches demonstrate promising potential for cardiac tissue engineering applications.

papers.title: Digital light processing of human-scale tissue-engineered heart valves
papers.abstract: Tissue engineered heart valves (TEHVs) could overcome the complications of current heart valve replacement, such as immunologic events, degenerative fibrocalcific changes, and patient-prosthesis mismatch. Digital light processing (DLP) 3D printing enables creation of complex geometries; however, suitable (bio)inks remain limited. Here, a composite ink comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA), gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA), and methacrylated quince seed mucilage (QSGM), termed GPQuin, was developed for DLP printing of human-scale TEHVs. GPQuin enabled fabrication of a trileaflet TEHV with separated leaflets and anatomically inspired sinuses. Micro-computed tomography revealed mean positive and negative surface deviations of +214 and -248 micrometers, respectively. The printed hydrogels exhibited a tensile modulus of 117.2 +/- 15.5 kPa, an ultimate tensile strength of 113.2 +/- 17.4 kPa, and an elongation at break of 75.3 +/- 2.3%. Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived valve cells attached to the hydrogel surfaces and remained predominantly viable over 14 days. After 12 weeks of subcutaneous implantation, the constructs showed a time-dependent inflammatory response. In a pulse duplicator under pulmonary loading, printed valves exhibited good cyclic leaflet opening and closing. Together, these findings establish GPQuin as a printable platform for human-scale valve scaffolds and support further investigation in heart valve tissue engineering.

papers.title: Continuous-flow synthesis and functionalization of gold nanoparticles for diagnostics and therapy
papers.abstract: Gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) are highly versatile platforms in nanomedicine, but their clinical translation is hin-dered by poor reproducibility and scalability during synthesis and surface functionalization, which are still pre-dominantly performed via manual batch protocols. To overcome these manufacturing bottlenecks, this work introduces a modular, continuous-flow millifluidic platform that integrates the automated synthesis of citrate-stabilized AuNPs and their subsequent multi-step surface modification within a single, streamlined pipeline. AuNPs of approximately 13 and 22 nm were reliably produced by adjusting the reagent stoichiometry. The flow-synthesized nanoconjugates showed hydrodynamic diameters comparable to those of the batch formulations, and comparable zeta potentials except for the PEG-containing ones. The platform's chemical flexibility was validated through two distinct surface modifications: an in-line covalent ligand exchange mediated by bidentate dithiolane anchors, and a salt-free, ultra-fast low-pH adsorption method. To benchmark diagnostic performance against established batch protocols, flow-modified AuNPs were evaluated in previously optimized SARS-CoV-2 RNA sensing systems, a cholesterol-driven molecular beacon assay and the CRISPR-Cas13a-mediated CAS-CADE platform, reproducing the response time, specificity, and colorimetric readout of their batch-produced counterparts without requiring tedious salt-aging steps. The same hairpin design was also adapted to a lateral flow format. For therapeutic purposes, two distinct classes of bioactive agents were evaluated: a small-molecule chemotherapeutic system co-loaded with SN38 and the nucleolin-targeting AS1411 aptamer, which exhibited potent anti-proliferative activity against triple-negative breast cancer cells (MDA-MB-231), and a nucleic acid-based platform functionalized with the antisense oligonucleotide ASO34a via the low-pH module, which trig-gered significant post-transcriptional gene silencing (achieving at least 30% luciferase knockdown at 24 hours in both breast and pancreatic PANC-1 cancer cell lines). This automated millifluidic platform demonstrates that complex, multi-component nanomaterial modifications can be successfully executed under continuous-flow configurations, reproducing the performance of established batch-synthesized diagnostic assays and yielding active therapeutic nanoconjugates. By coupling precise core synthesis with sophisticated surface engineering, this continuous manufacturing paradigm establishes a scalable and reproducible pathway to narrow the gap between laboratory-scale discovery and clinical manufacturing.

papers.title: VivoFemme: 3D printed human endometrium-on-chip with a thin membrane and gravity-driven perfusion
papers.abstract: Modeling endometrial function in vitro requires systems that support interactions among epithelial, stromal, and endothelial cells and allow their responses to hormonal and physical cues to be examined. Here, we present VivoFemme, an endometrium-on-chip platform that combines a capillary-pinned gelatin membrane, a stereolithographically 3D-printed microfluidic chip, and gravity-driven perfusion. Gelatin membrane retained on 3D-printed mesh supports separate independently accessible culture micro-channels. The membrane has approximately 10 micrometers thickness measured by cross-sections using scanning electron microscopy. Optimization of gelatin crosslinking conditions identified a formulation that maintained membrane integrity throughout the culture period. The microfluidic chip operates without external perfusion pumps or circulation tubing and supports primary human endometrial epithelial, stromal, and microvascular endothelial cells in mono-, co-, and tri-culture configurations. Compared with static culture, dynamic endothelial culture showed greater alignment along the flow axis and reduced permeability. Treatment with estradiol, medroxyprogesterone acetate, and cyclic adenosine monophosphate was accompanied by prolactin secretion and insulin-like growth factor-binding protein 1 staining, consistent with stromal decidualization. Prolactin and tracer permeability measurements differed across culture configurations. VivoFemme combines a thin gelatin interface with compartmentalized culture and gravity-driven perfusion to investigate how cellular composition and culture conditions influence endometrial responses.

papers.title: Tuning viral virulence and cytokine release enforces oncotropism and eliminates systemic toxicity: A framework for next-generation oncolytics
papers.abstract: Oncolytic virotherapy has long balanced safety and potency through permanent attenuation and, increasingly, constitutive inflammatory payloads. Yet attenuation can restrict replication in heterogeneous tumors, whereas unregulated cytokine expression can cause systemic toxicity and promote premature viral clearance. Here, we establish an alternative vaccinia framework that replaces fixed attenuation with reversible chemogenetic control of the essential replication gene E1L and coordinates replication with graded interleukin-12 (IL-12) expression through a hierarchical, drug-gated circuit. E1L control enabled inducible replication with no detectable consensus-level escape under tested selection conditions. Following intravenous administration, the fully induced virus maintained high intratumoral titers while reducing infectious-virus recovery across peripheral organs by orders of magnitude relative to thymidine-kinase-deleted vaccinia and the induced parent vector, without marked weight loss. Across syngeneic tumor models, dual induction prolonged survival and was associated with cytotoxic CD8+ T-cell and inflammatory macrophage states. This architecture establishes post-entry functional oncotropism through control of productive viral persistence.
